- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Location: review-blocked prompt-size log block around line 19029 (Review-blocked judge prompt size log)
  Issue: The wave judge path emits a `::warning::` above 950,000 characters (line ~20900) so future regressions are visible before they cross the hard 1 MB cap. The new inline review-blocked judge path logs the byte/char counts at line 19029 but has no equivalent 950K early-warning — it only fires the `::error::` and skips attempts at 1,048,576 characters. The README row for `JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` says "warns above 950,000 characters", which currently only matches the wave path; a single huge review-blocked prompt goes from "no log line" straight to the hard skip with no operator-visible warning beforehand.
  Suggested minimal fix: mirror the wave-judge 950,000-character warning (`echo "::warning::Review-blocked judge prompt for issue #${rb_issue} is ${RB_JUDGE_PROMPT_CHARS} characters ... close to or over codex's 1 MB stdin cap."`) immediately after the existing size log, gated by the same `> 950000` check the wave judge uses.
  Estimated lines changed: 3-5
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Location: _judge_truncate_pr_diff_file around line 232 (head -c fallback branch)
  Issue: The `head -c` fallback path returns 0 unconditionally when the command writes any output, even if `max_bytes` truncated the file mid-multibyte-character and the trailing byte is invalid UTF-8. The function comment says `sanitize_codex_prompt_file` strips an invalid trailing byte later, but `head -c` followed by `mv -f` on an already-1000-line-capped diff that contains multibyte chars would still let a partial code point through. The python3 path explicitly walks back the trailing continuation bytes (lines 224-227); the head -c fallback does not. Today this only matters in the rare "python3 missing" case, so it is defense-in-depth rather than a known runtime hit, but the two truncation paths now diverge on UTF-8 safety.
  Suggested minimal fix: tighten the head -c fallback to call the same python3 walker first and only fall back to raw head -c when python3 is genuinely absent, or document explicitly that the head -c path is allowed to produce invalid UTF-8 because `sanitize_codex_prompt_file` is responsible for cleanup.
  Estimated lines changed: 2-4
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Location: RB prompt assembly around line 18974-18977 (PR diff section in RB prompt)
  Issue: The inline review-blocked judge prompt now uses `printf '%s\n' "${PR_DIFF}"` (last run diff), removing the previous `head -1000 <<<` line cap. The wave judge still applies `head -n 500` before the byte cap, and the review-blocked path still applies `head -n 1000` before its byte cap, so the byte cap is the binding constraint for both. However, if the project-side JUDGE_PR_DIFF_MAX_BYTES is bumped very high (or set above the prompt's static-context budget) without raising the wave judge's 500-line cap, the prompt can still grow past the 1 MB cap from line count alone — the README mentions 524288 / 65536 defaults but not the relationship between the byte cap and the wave-only 500-line cap. This is more of an operator-facing note than a defect.
  Suggested minimal fix: note in the `JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` README row that the wave judge also has a 500-line cap (`head -n 500`) ahead of the byte cap, so a wave judge prompt is bounded by both `min(500_lines, JUDGE_PR_DIFF_MAX_BYTES_per_pr, JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES)` in bytes.
  Estimated lines changed: 1-2 (README only)
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
